ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is transformer T, and the secondary winding on the right is labeled U2; the upper end of the secondary is connected to the output terminal through a single diode VD; a filter capacitor C and load resistor RL are connected in parallel between the output terminal and the lower common line, and the output voltage UL is marked across RL. Reasoning: The problem gives U2 = 10 V, and capacitor C is open-circuited, so the filter branch does not function, and the remaining circuit is a single-diode half-wave rectifier circuit with a resistive load. According to the ideal half-wave rectification average output voltage relationship UL = 0.45U2, substituting U2 = 10 V gives UL = 0.45 × 10 V = 4.5 V.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: U2 is the transformer secondary voltage, VD is the only rectifying element, and RL is across the output UL; the capacitor C would normally smooth UL but is stated to be open. Use the text value U2 = 10 V RMS. Since C is open, no charge-holding/filter action occurs, so the load sees a half-wave rectified sine: positive half-cycle through VD, zero on the opposite half-cycle. Compute Vm = sqrt(2) × 10 V, then average over one period: UL = Vm/π = sqrt(2)×10/π ≈ 4.5 V.
